question: How many blocks are needed to pave a self-adjoint operator?
idea: Paving breaks an operator into diagonal blocks relative to a maximal commuting subalgebra so each block has controlled norm. The claim gives a block count proportional to the inverse square of the error tolerance. Its strong-operator version allows a compression approaching the identity; this qualification distinguishes it from unrestricted norm paving.
why: The study of collections of transformations acting on spaces of functions. These structures appear in quantum theory and infinite-dimensional geometry.

exactClaim: Proves that every self-adjoint element of a complex von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving relative to any maximal abelian subalgebra with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ blocks. The norm bound holds after compression by a projection arbitrarily close to the identity in the strong topology, resolving the Popa–Vaes quadratic paving conjecture.
